title: The dice
hook: Yudhishthira gambles a kingdom, then his brothers, then his wife

segments.voice: Yesterday: Pandava, the five sons of Pandu, raised with a hundred cousins and one throne between them. One house.

Just one more hand. One more spin, one more scroll, one more bet to win back what you lost on the last one. The Pandavas have done well. They've built a shining city of their own, Indraprastha, with a hall so magical that Duryodhana, visiting, mistakes a floor for a pool and a pool for a floor, and falls in, and people laugh. He goes home burning. His uncle Shakuni has an idea. Yudhishthira, the eldest Pandava, can't refuse a challenge. And Shakuni is a master of the dice.
screen: `JUST ONE MORE.` → `DURYODHANA FALLS IN THE POOL.` → `SHAKUNI, MASTER OF THE DICE.`

segments.voice: The invitation comes: a friendly game in the great hall at Hastinapura. Yudhishthira knows it's a trap. He says so, and goes anyway, because a king of his kind doesn't refuse a challenge. Shakuni throws for Duryodhana. In the popular telling his dice are loaded; the text simply says he's a master of deceit at the game. Yudhishthira stakes a jewel and loses. Gold. Chariots. His army. His treasury. His whole kingdom. Each time, he's sure the next throw will turn it. Then Shakuni asks: what else do you have? Yudhishthira stakes his brothers. The twins first, then Arjuna, then Bhima. He loses every one. He stakes himself, and loses. The hall is silent. There's one stake you haven't played, says Shakuni: your wife. And Yudhishthira, the man known for never lying, the son of dharma himself, stakes Draupadi. The dice fall. Vidura, the king's wise half-brother, has begged them all to stop the game, and no one listens. The other elders, the grandfather Bhishma, the teacher Drona, the blind king, let it go on. Look at who's throwing: not a fool, but the brother known for wisdom and honesty. That's the frightening part. The dice didn't ruin him in one throw. They ruined him one reasonable-looking bet at a time, each trying to fix the last, and at some point nobody, not even him, stops the hand. Tomorrow, what happened to Draupadi in that hall.
screen: `HE KNOWS IT'S A TRAP. HE GOES.` · `JEWELS, ARMY, KINGDOM, GONE.` · `HIS BROTHERS. HIMSELF. HIS WIFE.` · `NOBODY STOPS THE HAND.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands in your lap and feel them there, still. Think of a losing streak you kept betting on, maybe not money: an argument you kept doubling down on, a relationship you kept pouring into, a habit you kept saying you'd fix tomorrow, and notice the moment each time when the hand reached for the next throw. Then look at your hands now, resting; you can stop them.
The dice. A rigged game, a wise man who couldn't stop, and a kingdom, four brothers and a wife lost one throw at a time.
Your line: stop the hand. It was lost one throw at a time. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The dice game in the Sabha Parva is retold in homes, classical dance and theater, and readers often point to it as the moment the great war became hard to stop.

original.note: Sanskrit: dyuta, gambling with dice. The whole episode is called the dyuta.

trapdoor: what you thought: a foolish man gambles everything.
what it means: a wise man loses everything one reasonable-looking bet at a time, and nobody stops his hand.
what a scholar hears: dice games were part of old royal rituals, and Yudhishthira's refusal to decline a challenge follows the warrior code he held.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva (the hall at Indraprastha; Duryodhana's fall; the dice game, the dyuta)

notes: Duryodhana's fall in the maya-hall: the popular telling adds Draupadi laughing ('the son of a blind man is blind'); the script only says 'people laugh' because the attribution to Draupadi is disputed. Confirm.
Loaded dice: the text calls Shakuni a master of deceit at dice; loaded dice (sometimes made from his father's bones) are later popular tellings. Confirm framing.
The order of stakes (twins, Arjuna, Bhima, himself, Draupadi) follows the Sabha Parva as remembered; confirm.

Review edit: the earlier draft said the elders 'sat there and did nothing'; in the Sabha Parva Vidura protests strongly and urges the game be stopped, so the script now names him. Bhishma's and Drona's silence is mainly about Draupadi's question (tomorrow); confirm the wording here.
Trapdoor: dice in royal ritual (the rajasuya includes a ritual dice game); confirm the wording.
